version.philosophy: Procedure records and bindings are task knowledge that agents will follow, and once loaded they are history that is never rewritten. A record change is proven where it will live: the service must accept every version, reference and binding, a second load must write nothing, every binding must resolve, and the stored history it extends must be the one in the fixtures. A record never needs Go code to change; when it seems to, the change is not a records change.
version.method: Classify the changed files; check the new versions' content against the behavior they describe; load the fixtures into an isolated catalog twice and resolve every binding, also starting from a backup of the live catalog; then verify the commit through the shared verification at scope `records`, whose gate repeats the isolated load and replays the scripted procedural-memory loop. Load into the live catalog only after merge, and confirm that a second load writes nothing.
version.goal: Verify a change to Polaroid's procedure, repository or binding fixtures (examples/development, examples/task-aware) in isolated catalogs before it reaches the live one.

inputs.gate_commands: Passed to the verify reference, for example ["make records-check", "make demo"].
inputs.working_tree: Set by the agent at run time; passed to the verify reference.

applies_to: New procedures, appended versions (vN.revise.json with base_version N-1), origins, repositories and bindings under examples/development or examples/task-aware, with the documentation that describes them.
excluded: Editing or deleting a fixture version that is already stored anywhere: versions are never overwritten; append one instead.
Any change to Go code, scripts (including scripts/load-fixtures.sh and scripts/demo.sh), the Makefile or workflows: verify those through polaroid.change.focused or the full `verify-change` binding.
A binding revision after the first: scripts/load-fixtures.sh checks only revision 1, so a later revision is appended with the CLI (revise-binding) and stated in the evidence.
preconditions: The change is committed on a branch, or its working-tree state is recorded.
The live catalog can be backed up with `polaroid backup`.
contract.expected_outcome: Every changed file is applicable; the fixtures load into an empty catalog and into a copy of the live catalog, a second load writes nothing, and every binding resolves; the verify child is verified at the commit with scope `records`; after merge the live catalog holds the records and a second load writes nothing.
verification: Evidence lists the changed files with their classification.
`RECORDS_FROM=BACKUP make records-check` passed against a fresh backup of the live catalog, with its `records-check:` lines.
The verify child is verified at the commit; its checks ran the gate commands once.
After merge: the loader's report against the live catalog, and a second load reporting every procedure as matching, with nothing created or appended.
escalation: Any excluded file, or a record whose new behavior needs code to support it: stop, record nothing for this procedure, and use the procedure for the code (or `verify-change`). When unsure, use `verify-change`.
A conflict with the live catalog's history (a stored version differs from its fixture): never overwrite; append a new version that corrects it.
boundaries: Scope `records` covers the fixtures' acceptance, loading, references and bindings, and the scripted replay of the procedural-memory loop. It does not run the Go tests and never stands for full verification of the commit.
New versions are not selected over evidenced ones until they have evidence: a first run of a new version is chosen explicitly (get_graph for that version) and stated so.

Never loads into the live catalog before the change is merged, except when the commit itself is to be verified with the new versions (their first run): then load from that commit after the isolated checks pass, and say so. Never edits the live catalog except through the loader or the API.

steps.action: List the changed files against the merge base with main and classify each.

Read each new version against the commands, paths and behavior it describes, and check each against the repository (for example that a Make target or script it names exists and does what it says). References to shared procedures must reuse them by reference, not copy their instructions.

Back up the live catalog (`~/.local/bin/polaroid backup -dir DIR`), then run `RECORDS_FROM=BACKUP make records-check`: the fixtures must extend the live history, a second load must write nothing, and every binding must resolve.
Commit, then follow the `verify` reference at that exact commit with scope `records`.
Record this execution with the classification, the content checks, the live-copy check's output, and `children` linking the verify execution.

After merge, from a clean checkout of main, run `scripts/load-fixtures.sh examples/development` against the live service, then run it again and confirm it creates and appends nothing. For a new version's first use, select it explicitly with get_graph and say so.

version.revision_reason: Initial version, created for #65 (refs #62): record and binding changes had no procedure of their own; they were verified with the full Go gate, which never loaded them into a catalog holding the live history.
